input.quote: Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation, and the media on which the Software is distributed will be free from defects in materials and workmanship under normal use, for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period").
input.rationale: Section 7.3 gives a genuine conformance warranty against the Documentation plus a no-malicious-code warranty, and Section 7.3's second paragraph provides the full remedy set (correct, replace free of charge, and refund of all prepaid fees on termination if the breach cannot be corrected), so the remedy limb meets the playbook. The duration fails the fallback: the Warranty Period is only sixty (60) days and runs from the Effective Date rather than delivery/acceptance, with a hard December 31, 1999 sunset that could shorten it further given acceptance testing may run to that same date under Section 3.1. That is below the 90-day software floor, so we have extended it to twelve (12) months from acceptance and dropped the sunset. The disclaimer at p0084 is limited to implied warranties and does not swallow the express warranties, so no carve-out edit is needed.

proposal.summary: Extend the product warranty period from 60 days (with a Dec 31, 1999 sunset) to 12 months from acceptance.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Warranty Period to twelve (12) months running from acceptance and removed the fixed December 31, 1999 sunset, which could cut the warranty to almost nothing depending on delivery timing; our playbook expects a 12-month conformance warranty for software. The existing repair/replace/refund remedy is unchanged, and we can accept ninety (90) days from acceptance as a fallback.

ops.newText: for a period of twelve (12) months from the date Corio accepts the Software pursuant to Section 3.1 (the "Warranty Period")
